events.label: Natufian culture
events.blurb: Foragers in the Levant build some of the earliest permanent settlements.

events.label: Neolithic Jericho
events.blurb: Jericho becomes one of the oldest known towns, with a stone tower dated to about 8000 BCE.

events.label: Ghassulian culture
events.blurb: Chalcolithic farming and copper-working villages (dates approximate).

events.label: Early Bronze Age towns
events.blurb: Fortified towns spread across Canaan.

events.label: Amarna letters
events.blurb: Canaanite city rulers, including of Jerusalem, correspond with Egypt.

events.label: Merneptah Stele
events.blurb: An Egyptian inscription records a people named Israel in Canaan.

events.label: Philistine settlement
events.blurb: Aegean-origin migrants settle the southern coast; the name Philistia is the root of the later name Palestine.

events.label: Kingdoms of Israel and Judah
events.blurb: Highland kingdoms emerge from the local population; the extent of a united monarchy under David and Solomon is debated.

events.label: Tel Dan Stele
events.blurb: An Aramaic inscription refers to the 'House of David' (9th century BCE, approximate).

events.label: Assyria conquers Israel
events.blurb: The northern kingdom falls and much of its population is deported.

events.label: Babylon destroys Jerusalem
events.blurb: The First Temple is destroyed and Judeans are exiled to Babylon (586 or 587 BCE).

events.label: Persian rule; Judeans return
events.blurb: Cyrus allows exiles to return and rebuild the Temple.

events.label: Herodotus uses 'Palaistine'
events.blurb: The earliest known Greek use of the name for the region.

events.label: Alexander's conquest
events.blurb: The region passes to Greek rule.

events.label: Maccabean revolt
events.blurb: Judean revolt against the Seleucids leads to the Hasmonean kingdom.

events.label: Roman conquest
events.blurb: Pompey brings Judea under Roman control.

events.label: Destruction of the Second Temple
events.blurb: Rome destroys Jerusalem and the Temple during the First Jewish-Roman War.

events.label: Bar Kokhba revolt; Syria Palaestina
events.blurb: Rome suppresses the revolt, bars Jews from Jerusalem, and renames the province Syria Palaestina.

connections.note: Hadrian adopts the existing Greek regional name

events.label: Mishnah compiled
events.blurb: Rabbinic oral law is codified in the Galilee (c. 200 CE).

events.label: Christian holy sites built
events.blurb: Constantine's Church of the Holy Sepulchre and Bethlehem's Church of the Nativity are built.

events.label: Sasanian conquest
events.blurb: Persia briefly takes Jerusalem; Byzantium recovers it in 629.

events.label: Arab Muslim conquest
events.blurb: Caliph Umar takes Jerusalem (637 or 638); Arabization and Islamization proceed gradually over centuries.

events.label: Dome of the Rock
events.blurb: Umayyad caliph Abd al-Malik completes the shrine on the Temple Mount / Haram al-Sharif.

events.label: Crusader conquest
events.blurb: Crusaders take Jerusalem and kill much of its Muslim and Jewish population.

events.label: Saladin retakes Jerusalem
events.blurb: Ayyubid forces end Crusader rule in Jerusalem after Hattin.

events.label: Battle of Ain Jalut
events.blurb: Mamluks defeat the Mongols in the Jezreel Valley.

events.label: Ottoman conquest
events.blurb: The region becomes part of the Ottoman Empire for four centuries.

events.label: Jerusalem walls rebuilt
events.blurb: Suleiman the Magnificent builds the present Old City walls.

events.label: Zahir al-Umar in the Galilee
events.blurb: A local Arab ruler governs northern Palestine from Acre (dates approximate).

events.label: Revolt of 1834
events.blurb: Local revolt against Egyptian rule and conscription.

events.label: Ottoman Land Code
events.blurb: Land registration reform affects ownership of village farmland.

events.label: First Aliyah
events.blurb: Jewish immigrants from Eastern Europe found agricultural colonies.

events.label: First Zionist Congress
events.blurb: Herzl's movement calls for a Jewish home in Palestine.

events.label: Filastin newspaper
events.blurb: An Arabic newspaper in Jaffa promotes Palestinian identity and opposes Zionism.

events.label: Hussein-McMahon correspondence
events.blurb: British pledges of Arab independence; whether Palestine was included remains disputed.

events.label: Balfour Declaration
events.blurb: Britain supports a Jewish national home in Palestine while pledging not to prejudice the rights of non-Jewish communities.

events.label: British Mandate
events.blurb: The League of Nations confirms British rule with the Balfour policy included.

events.label: 1929 riots
events.blurb: Violence over the Western Wall kills 133 Jews and 116 Arabs, most of the Arabs killed by British forces.

events.label: 1936-39 Arab revolt
events.blurb: A general strike and armed uprising against British policy and Jewish immigration is suppressed.

events.label: Peel partition proposal
events.blurb: A British commission first proposes partition.

events.label: 1939 White Paper
events.blurb: Britain limits Jewish immigration and land purchases.

events.label: The Holocaust
events.blurb: Nazi Germany and its collaborators murder about six million Jews.

events.label: UN Partition Plan
events.blurb: Resolution 181 proposes Jewish and Arab states; Jewish leaders accept and Arab leaders reject it.

events.label: 1948 Arab-Israeli War
events.blurb: Civil war in Mandate Palestine becomes a regional war after Israel's founding.

events.label: Israel declares independence
events.blurb: The State of Israel is proclaimed as the Mandate ends.

events.label: 1948 Palestinian displacement
events.blurb: About 700,000 to 750,000 Palestinians flee or are expelled and are not allowed to return; Palestinians call it the Nakba.

events.label: Jewish emigration from Arab countries
events.blurb: Most Jews of the Arab world leave or are expelled over three decades, many to Israel.

events.label: 1949 Armistice Lines
events.blurb: The Green Line; Jordan holds the West Bank and Egypt holds Gaza.

events.label: Suez War
events.blurb: Israel, Britain and France attack Egypt.

events.label: PLO founded
events.blurb: An umbrella body for Palestinian nationalist groups.

events.label: 1967 War
events.blurb: Israel captures the West Bank, East Jerusalem, Gaza, Sinai and the Golan Heights.

events.label: UNSC Resolution 242
events.blurb: Calls for withdrawal from territories occupied and for recognized secure borders.

events.label: 1973 War
events.blurb: Egypt and Syria attack on Yom Kippur.

events.label: Egypt-Israel peace treaty
events.blurb: Israel returns Sinai in exchange for peace.

events.label: 1982 Lebanon War
events.blurb: Israel invades Lebanon; Phalangist militia kill hundreds to over 2,000 civilians at Sabra and Shatila.

events.label: First Intifada
events.blurb: A Palestinian uprising in the occupied territories.

events.label: Oslo Accords
events.blurb: Mutual recognition between Israel and the PLO and an interim self-government framework.

events.label: Rabin assassinated
events.blurb: An Israeli opponent of Oslo kills the prime minister.

events.label: Second Intifada
events.blurb: Roughly 1,000 Israelis and 3,000 Palestinians are killed (approximate).

events.label: Gaza disengagement
events.blurb: Israel withdraws settlers and troops from Gaza.

events.label: Hamas takeover and Gaza blockade
events.blurb: Hamas takes control of Gaza; Israel and Egypt impose a blockade.

events.label: 2014 Gaza war
events.blurb: About 2,250 Palestinians and 73 Israelis are killed.

events.label: Abraham Accords
events.blurb: Israel normalizes ties with several Arab states.

events.label: October 7 attack
events.blurb: Hamas-led attack on Israel kills about 1,200 people and takes 251 hostages.

events.label: Gaza war
events.blurb: Israeli military campaign in Gaza; the Gaza Health Ministry reports over 73,000 Palestinians killed by late 2026.

events.label: ICJ provisional measures
events.blurb: In South Africa v. Israel the court orders Israel to prevent genocidal acts; the case is pending.

events.label: ICC arrest warrants
events.blurb: Warrants are issued for Netanyahu, Gallant, and Hamas commander Mohammed Deif.

events.label: Israel-Iran war
events.blurb: Twelve days of Israeli strikes on Iran and Iranian missile fire on Israel.

events.label: UN Commission genocide finding
events.blurb: A UN Commission of Inquiry concludes Israel committed genocide in Gaza; Israel rejects the finding.

events.label: Western recognitions of Palestine
events.blurb: The UK, France, Canada and Australia recognize the State of Palestine.

events.label: October 2025 ceasefire
events.blurb: Hostages are exchanged for nearly 2,000 Palestinian prisoners; strikes in Gaza continue at a lower level.

events.label: 2026 Knesset election
events.blurb: Israel holds a scheduled general election; results are not included here.
